newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's strippable bonds without witholding tax.
newsitem.headline: Spain's strippable bonds without witholding tax.

text.p: Spanish Treasury said on Wednesday that legal entities will not have to pay the 25 percent witholding tax on new strippable bonds, expected to be issued from July this year.
"These (strippable) issuances will not have to pay witholding taxes when bought by legal entities. But this was already included in corporate tax law," Jaime Caruana told Reuter in a phone interview.

After press reports this morning, some dealers believed Spanish Treasury intended to eliminate witholding tax for all resident legal entities on bonds. But only strippable bonds are exempt from witholding tax.
Since 1991, foreign investors have not paid witholding taxes on Spanish bonos, while residents have to pay a 25 percent witholding tax.
This does not apply to short-term zero coupon bills.
